title: openai-compat: support Responses v1 variants, seed/determinism, and metadata passthrough; streaming & tools stability fixes
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Added: OpenAI Responses v1 variants support (seed/determinism and metadata passthrough). Fixed: streaming framing edge cases and tool-calling stability when partial chunks arrive. SDKs: Typescript typings and Python compat wrapper updates. Migration notes included in docs.
description:
Motivation:
As we expand our OpenAI compatibility layer to cover the newer Responses API variants, customers requested parity for seed/determinism flags and full metadata passthrough so telemetry and routing information survives through Redwood's compatibility wrapper. Additionally, there have been intermittent streaming stability issues when tool/function-calling payloads are streamed and partial frames arrive out of boundary; these manifest as truncated tool args or duplicate events in consumers. This PR implements Responses v1 variant handling, surfaces seed/determinism from incoming requests into deterministic path selection, ensures metadata is preserved on Responses objects (and carried to logs/telemetry), and fixes a few streaming framing edge cases uncovered during integration tests.

What this changes (high level):
- Add a Responses adapter that recognizes Responses API variants (v1, v1beta1) and normalizes fields into our internal response model.
- Preserve incoming request.metadata and attach it to the compat Responses object as-is. Metadata fields are opaque to the runtime but emitted to telemetry and available in SDK hooks.
- Wire seed/determinism flags: when a seed is present we route the request to the deterministic execution path and tag traces/metrics with deterministic=true. The compatibility layer accepts both `seed` and `determinism` top-level params and maps them to our internal run-time options.
- Streaming stability fixes: improved chunk framing and partial-frame buffering in openai_compat/streaming.py to avoid splitting function/tool call payloads across message boundaries. Added length-prefixed reassembly for multi-chunk tool-calls.
- SDK/Docs: Typescript SDK typings and Python wrapper updated to expose the new params. Docs updated with migration notes and examples for seed/determinism and metadata passthrough.
- Tests: added e2e integration tests that exercise deterministic routes, metadata propagation, and streaming reconnection semantics.

Compatibility notes and migration guidance:
- No breaking API changes: existing OpenAI-compat clients will continue to work. New behaviour only triggers when requests include `seed`/`determinism` or `metadata` fields.
- If customers relied on deduplication heuristics that ignored metadata, they may see different telemetry groupings once metadata passthrough is enabled. This is intentional and documented.
- For deterministic workloads, users should set `seed` (integer) or `determinism: true` per the docs. Deterministic routes will be scheduled on dedicated deterministic pools when configured (no change unless customers opt-in).

Rollout plan and risk mitigation:
- Feature flagged behind `openai_compat_responses_v1` for staged rollout. Default flag is enabled in canary and will be rolled to 50% of traffic for the first week.
- Added telemetry events for `compat_migration.v1` and `compat_deterministic.invoked` so we can monitor correctness and traffic split.
- The streaming reassembly logic is gated behind the same feature flag to allow quick rollback if we see any regressions.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for adapter normalization and seed mapping added.
- Integration tests added: test_responses_seed.py (deterministic path) and test_streaming_reconnect.py (streaming partial-chunk reassembly).
- Manual canary validation: exercised the SDK TypeScript example and the Python quickstart against local canary.

Notes for reviewers:
- The streaming changes are localized to openai_compat/streaming.py and the reassembly util; please pay attention to the buffering semantics and edgecases in comments.
- SDK typing changes in the TS SDK are minimal but needed to expose `metadata` on Response objects; confirm typings are backward compatible.

review_comments: Diego Rivera: Overall this looks great. Two asks: (1) validate seed is integer and bound it to a sensible range (2) ensure that deterministic tagging doesn't impact latency-critical routing. Can we add unit tests for validation?

Ava Chen (author): Added validation in responses_adapter.py and unit tests. Deterministic tagging only changes a routing tag; routing decision is still subject to existing latency SLO checks. Added comment and tests to ensure no latency regressions in canary.
Priya Nair: Please update the docs with migration steps and call out the telemetry change. Also ensure the SDK surfaces metadata as opaque so users don't rely on structure.
Ava Chen: Docs updated (redwood-docs/openai/responses.md) with migration steps and telemetry notes. SDK exposes metadata as `Record<string, any>` in TS and dict in Python; noted as opaque in docs.
Samir Patel: Found an edge-case where reconnects with overlapping chunks could produce duplicate tool-call args. Suggest adding a reassembly id and idempotency guard in streaming reassembly.
Ava Chen: Implemented reassembly id and idempotency check; added integration test for overlapped chunks (test_streaming_reconnect.py).
merge_summary: Squashed 7 commits into 1: add Responses v1 compatibility (seed/determinism, metadata passthrough), streaming reassembly improvements, SDK and docs updates. Canaried behind feature flag.

Monitor `compat_migration.v1` and `compat_deterministic.invoked` telemetry for first 72 hours
